_comment_key: Pins the extension ID to fllkfipajdahciclfcimfcenmfallgfm on every machine. Without it Chrome assigns a random id to each unpacked install, which would mean a separate CORS_ALLOW_EXTENSION_ORIGINS entry for every laptop in the company. The matching private key is extension-key.pem - keep it out of git, back it up, and reuse it when packing. Losing it means a new id and re-authorising the API.
name: PassM - Internal Password Manager
description: Internal company password manager. Fill and save credentials, search your vault and generate strong passwords.

_comment_permissions.storage: The item index (names, usernames, sites - never passwords) lives in chrome.storage.session, which is memory-backed and never written to disk. Sign-in tokens and settings use chrome.storage.local.
_comment_permissions.alarms: Proactive token refresh, vault auto-lock and clipboard auto-clear, all of which must survive the service worker being suspended.
_comment_permissions.activeTab + scripting: Fill a credential into the tab the user is looking at, only after they act.
_comment_permissions.contextMenus: Right-click menu for filling, copying and generating.
_comment_permissions.sidePanel: Full vault browser alongside the page.
_comment_permissions.clipboardWrite: Copy a password, then overwrite it after the configured delay.
_comment_permissions.offscreen: A service worker has no DOM and cannot reach the clipboard at all. A short-lived offscreen document performs the copy and the later auto-clear, then closes.
_comment_permissions.tabs: Read the active tab's URL to match vault entries to the site. Not used to track browsing - nothing is transmitted.
_comment_permissions.identity: Sign in with Google. Opens Google's own sign-in window (launchWebAuthFlow) and receives the ID token at https://<extension-id>.chromiumapp.org/, which must be an authorised redirect URI on the OAuth client. No Google data is read beyond the sign-in token.
_comment_permissions.host_permissions: Every http/https site. Needed for the browser's own HTTP sign-in box (webRequest.onAuthRequired only fires for sites the extension has host access to) - a vendor site can be anywhere. It adds no install warning: the content script already runs on every site, which Chrome already reports as access to all websites. It also covers the PassM server at whatever address it moves to.
_comment_permissions.webRequest + webRequestAuthProvider: Answer the browser's own Sign in dialog (HTTP Basic/Digest) with the login saved for that exact site - top-level pages only, once per request. See background/http-auth.ts.
_comment_permissions.exclude_matches: The browser new-tab pages and the extension stores. There is never a login form to fill on any of them, and injecting there only produced console noise - the new-tab document forbids some APIs by Permissions-Policy. Excluding them is both quieter and less surface.
_comment_permissions.content_scripts_all_frames: Login forms are frequently inside an iframe (Microsoft and Amazon both do this), so the detector has to run in child frames too.
